title: Lithium battery safety: power banks, tools and e-bikes
review_status: Source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
tldr: Follow the device and charger instructions. Stop using a battery with swelling, leakage, unusual heat, odor or noises. If it is smoking or burning, leave the area and call emergency services from a safe place; do not carry it through the home. Keep charging areas away from your escape route.
steps: Use the specified compatible charger and reputable, certified equipment. Do not improvise repairs to a damaged pack.
Keep batteries away from combustible materials, direct sun and hot vehicles. Follow the product temperature limits.
Stop using a device with unusual heat, changed shape, leaks, smells or sounds. Seek manufacturer or qualified repair advice rather than opening the pack.
Do not put lithium batteries in household trash. Ask the local battery collection service how it handles damaged batteries before transporting one.
sections: Editorial exercise: list where phones, power banks, tools and mobility batteries are normally charged. Mark any location that blocks a doorway or stair. Move routine charging to a suitable clear area according to the manufacturer; agree who checks that the right charger is used.

Compare the jobs you actually need a battery to do, cable compatibility, storage instructions and reputable certification information. Record the model and support contact. A larger battery adds cost and storage needs; test the smallest suitable option before expanding.
without_help: If a damaged battery cannot be assessed promptly, keep people away and avoid using or charging it. Smoke, fire or escalating heat calls for evacuation rather than waiting for a repair appointment.
household: Keep children away from chargers and damaged packs. Include e-bikes and mobility equipment in the escape plan; a battery or vehicle must not block the only exit.
pack_now: Model, charger specification, manufacturer contact and a separate flashlight. Keep emergency contacts accessible without the affected device.
next: Review charging locations, remove incompatible chargers from routine use and ask your local collection service about disposal arrangements.
watch: A battery exposed to flooding may need specialist handling. Do not test it by charging. Smoke and fire can make the surrounding air unsafe.
faqs: Can I fix a swollen battery?
Do not puncture, compress or open it. Stop using it and seek appropriate handling instructions.
decisions: Stop use and arrange qualified advice.
Leave, stay out and alert emergency services from a safe location.
scope: Civilian guidance using the linked U.S. reference. Local conditions and services differ. Household planning examples are Osprey Zero editorial suggestions; this is not a live alert or specialist certification.
